The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondent No.1 and 2 for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 12.11.2020 at about 6.30 p.m. deceased Anjanappa while returning to his home after attending his coolie work at Gottigere village along with his son Raghunatha, a motor cyclist bearing Reg.No. KA42EA 6867 came in high speed rash and negligently, endangering to human life and dashed against him and caused accident, so that, his son Raghunatha and other persons were taken him to CHC Hospital Kunigal, after first aid while shifting to Bengaluru for further treatment, he succumbed to death, dead body was taken to CHC Kunigal and post mortem is conducted, thereafter dead SCCH 5 body was taken to their native place and performed funeral ceremonies by spending more than Rs.2,00,000/.
3. At the time of accident, deceased was aged about 58 years, he was hale and healthy, working as gare coolie along with centering and bar bending work, thereby earning Rs.1,000/ to 1,200/.

Petitioner No.1 is his wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are his sons, petitioner No.4 is mother of the deceased Anjanapa, due to sudden death of the Anjanappa, petitioners have lost their bread,
suffered physically and mentally, due to the said accident, crime No.277/2020 is registered before Kunigal Police against the rider of the motor cycle for the offences punishable under Sec.279,
304(A) of IPC.

R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the vehicle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, hence prays to allow SCCH 5 the petition and grant compensation of Rs.40,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.

R2/insurer has also appeared through his advocate and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, further taken contention that, motor cyclist had no driving license at the time of accident, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act, claim made by the petitioner is higher side, hence petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:
SCCH 5 ::ISSUES::
1.
Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Late.Anjanappa, S/o.

Late. 
Yalavaiah died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.11.2020 at about 6.30 p.m. near Channathimmanapalya Gate, near Lokesh Residence due to rash and negligent riding of two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA42EA6867 by its rider, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.2 has deposed his evidence as PW1, petitioner No.1 is examined as PW2 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, R1 has not contested the petition, R2 has not given evidence inspite of giving sufficient opportunities.
SCCH 5 8.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9.
Issue No.1:
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.2 has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chiefexamination he has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1. copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot panchanama is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of seizure panchanama is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of inquest panchanama is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of P.M.

There is no cross examination with regard to place, date and time of the accident, further denied that, he is not eyewitness to this incident.
Further there is no crossexamination about negligency either of the parties.

10. Further petitioner No.1 has deposed her evidence as PW2, There is no crossexamination with regard to place, date and time of the accident, further denied that, she is not eyewitness to this incident.
Further there is no crossexamination about negligency of either of the parties.
11. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence to deny the case of the petitioners, further charge sheet is against rider of the motor cycle.
Hand sketch map marked as Ex.P.4 speaks that, on side of the passage road this accident is occurred.
It is defence of SCCH 5 the respondents that this motor cycle has not caused the accident, but there is no counter evidence to prove that, which vehicle has caused this accident.
Further death in the road traffic accident is not disputed, charge sheet is only against the rider of the motor cycle.

Under such circumstances, this tribunal is of the opinion that,
evidence available on record is sufficient to hold that very accident is occurred due to negligency of rider of the motor cycle on the alleged place, date and time of the accident.
Hence believing the version of the petitioner, I have answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was aged APSRTC Bus out 58 years as on the date of accident.

To prove the said fact, they have produced copy of aadhar card of deceased marked as Ex.P.10, accordingly he is born in the year 1961 and the SCCH 5 alleged accident is occurred on 2020, accordingly relying on Ex.P.10 age of the deceased is considered about 59 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 9 is applicable with reference to Sarla Verma case.
13. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as gare coolie along with centering and bar bending work and earning Rs.1,000/ to Rs.1,200/ per day.

There are no documents on record, under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.14,500/ p.m.

14. Further petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are children, petitioner No.4 is mother of the SCCH 5 deceased Anjanappa, in this regard they have produced aadhar card of petitioner No.1 to 4 marked as Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.14, copy of ration card marked as Ex.P.16, hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 4 to 6 persons, then 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/4th of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

15. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 10% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged upto 60 years, in case of self employed person or person having fixed salary as future prospects.

with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
20.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.2312202510108200000, which is valid for the period from 17.11.2018 to 16.11.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 12.11.2020, it reveals that, as on the date of accident insurance policy was in force.
There is no charge sheet against rider of the motor cycle by name Mahadeva for the offences punishable under Sec.3 R/w. Sec.181 of SCCH 5 M.V.Act.
hence naturally liability shall go against R2, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

Inview of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,81,896/ (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Eighty One Thousand Eight Hundred Ninety Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
SCCH 5 The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 50:10:10:30 in the award amount.

The Petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

SCCH 5 The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 50:10:10:30 in the award amount.

The Petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
